unit.title: Shortest and best: puzzles, paths, packing

lesson.title: The shortest way
lesson.subtitle: Add up the roads, and settle the closest place first

video.title: The shortest way
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor Eze — your science teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talks to the student)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor beside a big paper map of villages and roads pinned to the classroom wall.
scenes.animation: Roads light up one by one; a raindrop falls on the bridge.
scenes.narration: From your home to school, there are many ways to go. Some roads are long, some are short, and one bridge floods when it rains. Which way is the shortest?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: find the shortest way, step by step.

scenes.visual: A road with a number tag; two roads joined, their numbers added with a plus.
scenes.animation: Numbers slide together and add up.
scenes.narration: On a map, each road has a number: how many kilometres long it is. To find how long a way is, add up its roads. The way with the smallest total is the shortest.

scenes.visual: Two routes on the map; the bendy one wins with a star.
scenes.animation: Each route lights up as it is added; the star pops on 13.
scenes.narration: The way through Bora looks straight: five and ten make fifteen. The way through Tala, Kesi and Mina has more bends: four, three, two and four make thirteen. Thirteen is shorter!

scenes.visual: Numbered steps beside the map; home glows with a 0.
scenes.animation: Steps appear one by one as they are said.
scenes.narration: Here’s a trick that always works. Give each place a number: the shortest way you’ve found so far. Each turn, settle the waiting place with the smallest number. Then look at its roads, and give its neighbours smaller numbers if you can.

scenes.visual: Amina points at two villages with number badges 5 and 6. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Bora has five, and Rubi has six. Which one do you settle first?

scenes.visual: Bora gets a lock; the numbers spread across the map until the school shows 13.
scenes.animation: Locks appear village by village; the school lights up.
scenes.narration: Bora, because five is smaller than six. Nothing can make Bora closer than five now. Keep going until the school is settled: thirteen kilometres.

scenes.visual: Water covers the bridge; a new route through Rubi and Sana draws itself.
scenes.animation: Waves rise over the bridge; the new route lights up.
scenes.narration: After heavy rain, the bridge between Kesi and Mina is closed. Start again from home with the same trick. Now the shortest way goes through Rubi and Sana: fourteen kilometres.

scenes.visual: A small robot on a grid with walls; it walks around the walls to a star.
scenes.animation: The robot moves square by square to the star.
scenes.narration: Robots and map apps find shortest ways too. A robot on a grid counts squares, and walls block its path. The fewest moves is its shortest way.

scenes.visual: Children walking to school from different villages; one has a much longer path.
scenes.animation: Paths draw from each village; the longest one is circled.
scenes.narration: Some children walk much farther to school than others. When grown-ups plan a new road or bridge, they can ask: who walks the farthest? A fair plan helps them too.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: the village map, numbers in circles, a finger tapping.
scenes.animation: Villages settle one by one; the shortest way lights up.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: The shortest way to school
scenes.narration: In the app, tap Home, then always tap the waiting village with the smallest number. When the school is settled, the shortest way lights up. Then flood the bridge, and try again.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor points at the flooded bridge on the map. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The bridge is flooded. Which way is the shortest now?

scenes.visual: Summary lines and an orange takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Through Rubi and Sana: fourteen kilometres. Remember: add up the roads. Settle the smallest number first. And when a road closes, find a new way.

scenes.visual: A pupil drawing a map with a pencil: home, a shop, a well, school, numbers on the roads.
scenes.animation: Roads draw themselves; one road gets a cross.
scenes.narration: Try it yourself: draw a map of your way to school or to the market, with a number on each road. Find the shortest way with the trick. Then close one road, and find the new way.

checkpoints.prompt: Bora has 5 and Rubi has 6. Which do you settle first?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — always settle the smallest number first. Nothing can make Bora closer than 5 now.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — settle the smallest number first: Bora, 5. Then its number can’t change.

checkpoints.prompt: The bridge is flooded. Which way is the shortest now?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 6 + 5 + 3 = 14 km through Rubi and Sana, shorter than both 15 km ways.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — add the roads: through Rubi and Sana is 6 + 5 + 3 = 14 km. The other two are 15 km.
